summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best performers are short, surprising 'X doesn't do what you think' videos about hands-on gadgets like robots, clap switches and mics, which earn the most likes, saves and shares. Everyday-object explainers (taps, lifts, smoke alarms, doors, touchscreens) and 'How does X know...?' question titles get far fewer views and almost no saves.
winningPattern: Hindi videos about a maker-style gadget or robot (clap switch, gyro robot, line follower, mic, PIR/IR sensor) with a surprising negation hook like 'X ke paas Y nahi hota' or 'X sunta/dekhta nahi, bas Z karta hai'. Titles are short, punchy statements with one emoji, not generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' questions. Posted on Instagram first, where reach is 1,000-1,200 per video; YouTube only occasionally breaks 500 (gyro, clap switch, PIR).
doMore: Use the negation hook: 'Yeh X nahi karta, bas Y karta hai' on maker gadgets and robots
Make series of the proven topics: clap switch, gyro/balancing robot, line follower, mic vs speaker, PIR sensor
End with a build-it or save-this payoff (pin names, tiny circuit) to drive saves and shares
Make the robot or gadget visibly do something in the first second, then explain why
Post on Instagram first and repost to YouTube with a more searchable title, since YouTube views are weak and uneven
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' titles on everyday objects like taps, lifts, mall doors and smoke detectors
Posting near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector, two IR sensor, two tap videos) within days of each other
Publishing English or untested-language videos with no Instagram version
